points.description: States that the learning rate controls the step size, and so the speed of convergence. A small learning rate gives slow (overdamped) convergence. A large learning rate gives faster but oscillating or zigzagging (underdamped) convergence. Equivalent wording earns the mark.
points.partial_credit: Half mark if the answer only says the learning rate controls step size or speed of convergence, without describing what happens at low versus high values.

points.description: Names the danger: if the learning rate is too large (above a critical value), learning becomes unstable or diverges. Equivalent wording such as 'overshoots and fails to converge' earns the mark.
